solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ruined health on diet eating duck dish

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the duck letter goes inside the reworked letters
ruined means wrecked, so the letters of health on diet are rearranged

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so it gives O

explanation.surface: Someone's health has been wrecked by a diet that includes eating duck.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of nothing, which looks like the letter O. Toad in the hole is a British dish of sausages baked in batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Toad in the hole is a traditional British meal of sausages cooked in Yorkshire pudding batter.

clue.text: Branch manager Greene tours abroad

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters of Greene and tours are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company's branch manager named Greene travels overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch manager' reads as a business title, but the branches are those of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree surgeon prunes and cares for trees, managing their limbs: a witty sense of branch manager.

clue.text: Pervasive quality of first-class travellers

parts.note: A is used for first-class, as in A1 or grade A
the Roma are a travelling people

explanation.surface: Something hangs about first-class passengers on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive smell, and figuratively an atmosphere or quality that surrounds something.

clue.text: What you do in pub close to crapulent bankrupt

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the solver's activity goes inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
what you, the crossword solver, do is solve the clues

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the last letter of crapulent

explanation.surface: Someone drinking in a pub, close to being sick from overindulgence, is going broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What you do' addresses the solver, who solves; crapulent means ill from too much drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolvent means unable to pay one's debts, the same state as being bankrupt.

clue.text: You shouldn't have clipped sea monkey

parts.note: said on receiving a gift, a polite form of thanks, and ta is British slang for thanks

indicators.note: clipped means cut short, so the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: marine means of the sea

explanation.surface: A gift of a sea monkey prompts the polite protest that you shouldn't have.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is informal British for thank you. 'sea monkey' looks like one thing, but sea is wordplay and monkey the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamarin is a small South American primate related to the marmoset.

clue.text: Tory no more whose time has passed

definitions.note: a noun phrase in the answer, a person whose prison term is over

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was
Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician who has had their day and is out of office.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a politician past their prime; the 'time' is a prison sentence served.
explanation.definitionFit: An ex-con is a former convict, someone who has done their time in prison.

clue.text: Frau converted, absorbed in additional prayer

indicators.note: absorbed in means held inside, so the reworked letters go within the word for additional

parts.note: other means additional, as in other reasons

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the letters of Frau are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German woman has converted to a new faith and is absorbed in extra prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Frau is German for a married woman; 'converted' looks like religious conversion but signals rearranging her letters, which are then 'absorbed in' the word for additional.
explanation.definitionFit: Our Father is the opening of the Lord's Prayer and is used as a name for it.

clue.text: Measure pain after leaving hospital

indicators.note: after leaving means the hospital letter has gone from the word for pain

parts.note: hell can mean torment or pain, as in going through hell
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone takes stock of the pain after being discharged from hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old unit of length for measuring cloth, about 45 inches in England.

clue.text: Backed augury one found in movie?

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the word for augury is read in reverse

parts.note: an omen is an augury, a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: A reversed prophecy turns up in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the play on the film title Finding Nemo.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemo is the clownfish who is found in the Pixar film Finding Nemo.

clue.text: Cécile is dancing with Mr D?

definitions.note: the capital letter D is shaped like a half circle, flagged with a question mark as a definition by example

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters of Cécile is and Mr are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman called Cécile is dancing with a man, Mr D.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr D' looks like a name, but Mr is fodder and D a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter D is a straight line closed by a half circle, so it pictures a semicircle.

clue.text: One attacking a crew member reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so the answer sounds like the phrase meaning a crew member

parts.note: a sailor is a member of a ship's crew

explanation.surface: Someone attacked a crew member, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailer is an assailant, a person who assaults or attacks someone.

clue.text: Tight times just around the corner

parts.note: near means stingy or tight with money
by means multiplied by, as in three by four

explanation.surface: Hard times are close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby means close at hand, a short distance away, like a shop around the corner.

clue.text: Dear Welsh leopard destroyed residence

parts.note: bach is a Welsh term of endearment, like dear

indicators.note: destroyed means broken up, so the letters of leopard are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dear Welsh leopard has wrecked someone's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear Welsh' looks like 'Dear Welsh leopard', but only the first two words give the Welsh endearment bach.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor pad is a flat or house lived in by a single man, a residence.

clue.text: High-street trader avoiding alcohol daily

parts.note: dry means teetotal or alcohol-free
in Britain a daily is a cleaner who comes in every day

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who avoids alcohol every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like an adverb, but it is a noun: a daily is a domestic cleaner in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry cleaner is a shop, typically on a town's main shopping street, that cleans clothes without water.

clue.text: Firms criticise one blocking move towards south

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, so these letters go inside the word for move towards

parts.note: to come is to move towards
to pan is to criticise harshly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Businesses criticise one person who blocks a move towards the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Companies and firms are both businesses, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Agent to slow insect devouring pitch

indicators.note: devouring means swallowing up, so the word for pitch goes inside the insect

parts.note: a red ant is an insect
tar is pitch, a black sticky substance

explanation.surface: A substance to slow down an insect that eats tar.
explanation.definitionFit: A retardant is a substance that delays or slows a process, as in fire retardant.

clue.text: Rhine wine or pop?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a white wine from the Rhineland, in Germany
second meaning: pop is slang for pawn

explanation.walkthrough: The surface offers a choice of drinks, wine or a fizzy soft drink; pop is in fact slang for pawning.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is a German white wine, and to hock is informal for pawning an item, as pop is.

clue.text: Goethe for one discarding an original thought

indicators.note: discarding means throwing away, so the letters of an are dropped

parts.note: Goethe was a German poet, so he is an example of a German

explanation.surface: Goethe throws away an original idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is the starting point from which something develops, as in the germ of an idea.

clue.text: Sons leaving to track bird and rabbit directly

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so the letter for sons is dropped

parts.note: to stalk is to track someone
S is the abbreviation for son or sons
a turkey is a bird

explanation.surface: Sons go off to hunt a bird and a rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' is British slang for talk (from rhyming slang rabbit and pork), not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk turkey is an idiom for speaking frankly, so to chatter in a direct way.

clue.text: Beat with undesirable acceleration in dance

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
bad means undesirable
a is the symbol for acceleration in physics

explanation.surface: A rhythm that speeds up in an unwelcome way during a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast Brazilian dance performed by couples, popular in 1989.

clue.text: Really popular female performance

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A genuinely popular show by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In fact is used to emphasise truth, meaning actually or in reality.

clue.text: Motorist finally learned to put foot down

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

parts.note: the last letter of Motorist
to read a subject is to study it, so read means learned

explanation.surface: A driver at last learned to accelerate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put foot down' suggests accelerating a car, but it means to step.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is to walk or step, putting one's foot down on the ground.

clue.text: Old woman hot in desert run

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, an old woman

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the hot letter goes within the words for desert

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert or betray them
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An elderly woman feels the heat while out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a sandy place, but it is the verb, giving RAT ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a long-distance running race of about 26 miles.

clue.text: Host hasn't run very small outfit

indicators.note: hasn't means lacks, so the letter for run is removed

parts.note: a host is a large crowd, a throng
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A party host who hasn't run is wearing a skimpy outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' suggests someone giving a party; here it means a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a skimpy garment, either brief underwear or swimwear, so a tiny outfit.

clue.text: Wants facts about English team heading for relegation

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for facts is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: data are facts or information
a side is a team

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of relegation

explanation.surface: Facts about an English team that is heading for relegation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for relegation' sounds like a team about to be demoted, but it just gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderata are things wanted or needed; the Latin plural means things desired.

clue.text: Purpose Kennedy periodically reveals

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so alternate letters of Kennedy are taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Kennedy

explanation.surface: Kennedy now and then reveals his aim.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is an aim or goal, as in a means to an end.

clue.text: Surgical procedure breaks bone: my mistake!

indicators.note: breaks means splits open, so the procedure goes inside the word for bone

parts.note: os is the Latin and anatomical word for bone
op is short for operation

explanation.surface: A surgeon breaks a bone during an operation and apologises.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is an exclamation used on making an error, an admission of a slip.

clue.text: Poor dealt with for fencing blue Aston Martin?

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the word for dealt with surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: to do a task is to deal with it, so did means dealt with
blue means sad or down
the Vantage is a model of Aston Martin sports car, so the question mark flags an example

explanation.surface: Someone poor makes do with a sad Aston Martin they cannot replace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link here. The Vantage is a real Aston Martin model, hence the question mark marking a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Disadvantaged means lacking money and opportunities, so it describes people who are poor.
